content:
Maya Chen: quick heads-up: we're missing a safe default for the console 'capture trace' flow. current inspect tokens leak raw payloads for too long. we need a short TTL + stronger redact-by-default policy 
Kevin Ortiz: ok. are we talking per-route on-demand inspect tokens? 
Maya Chen: yes. goal: one-click capture but masked unless explicitly escalated with audit + approval. 
Olivia Park: agree. product wants frictionless debug, security wants minimal exposure. can we show redaction state in the UI? 
Samir Patel: UX idea: badge that shows Masked / De-identified / Raw. clicking Raw opens an approval modal requiring owner + reason. one-click still possible after approval. 
Priya Desai: security reqs: every raw unmask must record who, why, TTL, and request hash. add per-tenant rate limits and quota on raw tokens. 
Maya Chen: propose defaults: mode=masked, inspect_token_ttl=300s (5m), escalation requires approval & audit_hmac, sticky only for session, not persisted. 
Kevin Ortiz: HMAC audit: use tenant KMS to sign (route_id + ts + nonce) so logs only have non-reversible HMACs. salt per-tenant, rotated. 
Olivia Park: and masked mode = run PII heuristics + truncate long completions (>512 tokens) and replace excess with checksum. 
Samir Patel: entitlement split: view-only (SRE) vs download-raw (SOC/legal). show entitlements inline on modal. 
Priya Desai: storage: immutable audit stream, write-once, encrypted, retention 1y min. S3 -> Glacier with signed entries. 
audit-bot: auto-generated note: created audit stream ticket #INF-9123 - audit cfg pending. 
Maya Chen: operational detail: sampling-on-demand should annotate events with inspect_token_id so we can revoke at read-time. don't try to mutate stored blobs. 
Kevin Ortiz: revoke = check token validity & entitlement at read-time, redact if invalid. this avoids expensive blob mutations. 
Olivia Park: UX: console shows badge + TTL countdown. if token revoked, UI replaces raw content with masked view and reason for revocation. 
Samir Patel: rollout plan proposal: 1) server-side default masked + 5m TTL; 2) internal console canary with UI badges & approval modal; 3) quota enforcement + telemetry alerts; 4) broaden rollout after legal signoff. 
Priya Desai: quota math: charge tokens ~= estimated tokens sampled. per-tenant daily cap + global guardrail. fallback to masked when exceeded. 
Maya Chen: code-proto for inspect_policy (rough): 
```
{"inspect_policy": {"default_mode": "masked", "token_ttl_seconds": 300, "escalation": {"requires_approval": true, "approval_ttl_seconds": 600, "audit_hmac": true}, "quota": {"per_tenant_daily_tokens": 100000, "global_failback": "masked"}}} 
``` 
Olivia Park: nice. clarify masked behavior and checksum replacement for long generations. 
Kevin Ortiz: implementation note: store hashed fingerprints (HMAC) not raw ids. KMS holds salt; only HMACs in logs. 
Samir Patel: and ensure telemetry schema includes inspect_mode + inspect_token_id so downstream tools can filter & alert. 
Priya Desai: enforcement: quota checks at token issuance time. if issuing would exceed quota, return masked token and log attempted escalation. 
Maya Chen: can someone own an RFC that covers config keys, KMS/HMAC spec, UI mock, audit retention and quota calc? 
Olivia Park: I'll draft the UI/UX mock and the modal copy. 
Kevin Ortiz: I'll detail KMS usage, HMAC scheme, and rotation plan. 
Samir Patel: I'll write rollout steps and entitlement matrix. 
Priya Desai: I'll own audit retention, immutable stream design, and quota enforcement logic. 
Maya Chen: thanks all. tagging @Olivia Park @Kevin Ortiz @Samir Patel @Priya Desai 440 sync tomorrow 11am PT to finalize RFC. 
Olivia Park: ack 
Kevin Ortiz: ack 
Samir Patel: ack 
Priya Desai: ack 
Maya Chen: final note: avoid logging model completions by default. telemetry should prefer prefix-only or checksum placeholders unless raw completions are explicitly requested and approved. 
Maya Chen: end thread - leaving a short checklist in the RFC draft.
